q-byzanz-01#question: On the site of which Greek city did Constantine the Great dedicate his new capital in 330?
q-byzanz-01#explanation: Constantinople was built on the site of ancient Byzantium on the Bosporus, after which the empire was later called the "Byzantine Empire".
q-byzanz-02#question: In which year was Constantinople dedicated as the new capital?
q-byzanz-02#explanation: Constantine the Great dedicated the city on 11 May 330.
q-byzanz-03#question: What did the inhabitants of the Byzantine Empire call themselves?
q-byzanz-03#explanation: The Byzantines regarded themselves as Romans; the name "Byzantine Empire" was coined only by early modern scholars.
q-byzanz-04#question: Which language became the language of court and administration in the 7th century?
q-byzanz-04#explanation: Under Heraclius, Greek, the language of the majority in the East, finally replaced Latin as the official language.
q-byzanz-05#question: What happened in 395 after the death of Emperor Theodosius I?
q-byzanz-05#choices.1: The empire was divided between his sons into a western and an eastern half
q-byzanz-05#choices.2: Constantinople was captured by the Goths
q-byzanz-05#choices.3: Rome became the sole capital again
q-byzanz-05#explanation: Arcadius received the East and Honorius the West; afterwards the two halves of the empire drifted further and further apart.
q-byzanz-06#question: Roughly how long did the Eastern Roman Empire last after the end of the Western Empire in 476?
q-byzanz-06#explanation: The Eastern Roman Empire lasted until the conquest of Constantinople in 1453, almost a thousand years longer than the West.
q-byzanz-07#question: Which fortifications protected Constantinople on its landward side from the 5th century?
q-byzanz-07#explanation: The land walls completed under Theodosius II around 413 were not taken by storm by any attacker for more than a thousand years.
q-byzanz-08#question: What did the Council of Chalcedon decide in 451?
q-byzanz-08#choices.0: The primacy of the pope over all bishops
q-byzanz-08#choices.1: That Christ is true God and true man in two natures
q-byzanz-08#choices.3: The division of the empire into themes
q-byzanz-08#explanation: The council taught that Christ has two natures, without confusion and without division; many Christians in Egypt and Syria rejected this.
q-byzanz-09#question: Where does the name of the Nika riots of 532 come from?
q-byzanz-09#choices.1: From the city of Nicaea, where they began
q-byzanz-09#choices.3: From the goddess of victory, whose statue was toppled
q-byzanz-09#explanation: The rioters shouted "Nika!", "Conquer!", the cry usually used to cheer on the charioteers in the Hippodrome.
q-byzanz-10#question: Which two circus factions joined forces against the emperor in the Nika riots?
q-byzanz-10#explanation: The Blues and the Greens were supporters of the racing teams in the Hippodrome and at the same time influential political groups.
q-byzanz-11#question: Which general conquered the Vandal kingdom in North Africa for Justinian in 533/534?
q-byzanz-11#explanation: Belisarius landed in North Africa in 533, took Carthage and forced King Gelimer to surrender in 534.
q-byzanz-12#question: Against which people did Byzantium fight for Italy from 535 to 554?
q-byzanz-12#explanation: Belisarius and Narses won Italy back from the Ostrogoths in a long war; in 568 the Lombards then invaded.
q-byzanz-13#question: Which disease struck the Byzantine Empire from 541 onwards?
q-byzanz-13#explanation: The Plague of Justinian was the first known plague pandemic; DNA finds have identified the pathogen Yersinia pestis.
q-byzanz-14#question: According to Procopius, how did silkworms reach the Byzantine Empire?
q-byzanz-14#choices.0: As a gift from the Chinese emperor
q-byzanz-14#choices.1: Through a peace treaty with Persia
q-byzanz-14#choices.2: Monks smuggled their eggs in hollow canes
q-byzanz-14#choices.3: Arab merchants sold them in Alexandria
q-byzanz-14#explanation: Around 552 monks secretly brought silkworm eggs to Constantinople, after which the empire developed its own silk production.
q-byzanz-15#question: Which part of Justinian's legal compilation contains excerpts from the writings of Roman jurists?
q-byzanz-15#explanation: The Digest, also called the Pandects, published in 533, collected excerpts from the works of classical Roman jurists.
q-byzanz-16#question: Which historian described Justinian's wars and also wrote a spiteful "Secret History" about the emperor?
q-byzanz-16#explanation: Procopius praised Justinian in his official works but attacked him and Theodora sharply in the Secret History, which became known only later.
q-byzanz-17#question: Which emperor defeated the Persian army near Nineveh in 627?
q-byzanz-17#explanation: Heraclius led a daring campaign into the Persian heartland and forced a peace on the Sasanians in 628.
q-byzanz-18#question: Which relic did Heraclius bring back to Jerusalem in 630 after his victory over the Persians?
q-byzanz-18#choices.0: The bones of the Apostle Peter
q-byzanz-18#explanation: The Persians had carried off the Cross from Jerusalem in 614; Heraclius solemnly returned it in 630.
q-byzanz-19#question: In which battle was a Byzantine army defeated by the Arabs in 636, leading to the loss of Syria?
q-byzanz-19#explanation: After the defeat at the Yarmuk, a tributary of the Jordan, Heraclius gave up Syria.
q-byzanz-20#question: Which province, the granary of Constantinople, did the Arabs conquer between 640 and 642?
q-byzanz-20#explanation: With Egypt the empire lost its richest province and the capital's most important source of grain.
q-byzanz-21#choices.1: An incendiary weapon that kept burning even on water
q-byzanz-21#choices.3: The eternal flame in the Hagia Sophia
q-byzanz-21#explanation: The liquid, sprayed from tubes, set enemy ships alight and was almost impossible to put out.
q-byzanz-22#question: To whom does tradition attribute the invention of Greek fire?
q-byzanz-22#explanation: According to the chronicler Theophanes, Kallinikos brought the weapon to Constantinople around 672; its composition remained secret.
q-byzanz-23#question: What was the Byzantine Iconoclast controversy about?
q-byzanz-23#choices.0: The right to depict emperors on coins
q-byzanz-23#choices.3: Whether religious images may be venerated
q-byzanz-23#explanation: Opponents of images considered the veneration of icons idolatry, while their supporters saw icons as a path to the holy.
q-byzanz-24#question: Under which emperor did the Iconoclast controversy begin in the 8th century?
q-byzanz-24#explanation: Leo III turned against the veneration of images around 726/730; how far he went is disputed.
q-byzanz-25#question: Which council permitted the veneration of images again in 787?
q-byzanz-25#explanation: At the instigation of Empress Irene, the Second Council of Nicaea declared the veneration of images legitimate.
q-byzanz-26#question: Which empress had her own son blinded in 797 and then ruled alone?
q-byzanz-26#explanation: Irene had Constantine VI blinded and, until 802, became the first woman to rule the empire alone.
q-byzanz-27#question: With which feast does the Orthodox Church commemorate the end of Iconoclasm in 843?
q-byzanz-27#explanation: On the first Sunday of Lent the Orthodox Church celebrates the restoration of the veneration of images by Empress Theodora.
q-byzanz-28#question: To which country did Cyril and Methodius travel as missionaries in 863?
q-byzanz-28#explanation: Prince Rastislav of Great Moravia had asked the emperor for teachers who could preach in the Slavic language.
q-byzanz-29#question: Which script did Cyril himself create for the Slavic language?
q-byzanz-29#explanation: Cyril developed the Glagolitic script; the Cyrillic script named after him emerged only later among his disciples in Bulgaria.
q-byzanz-30#question: In which language did Cyril and Methodius celebrate the liturgy with the Moravians?
q-byzanz-30#explanation: The brothers translated liturgical texts into Slavic, which Frankish clergy fiercely opposed.
q-byzanz-31#question: Which city did Cyril and Methodius, the Apostles to the Slavs, come from?
q-byzanz-31#explanation: Many Slavs lived in the region around Thessaloniki, so the brothers knew the language from childhood.
q-byzanz-32#question: Which Bulgarian ruler was baptized around 864 and adopted Christianity from Byzantium?
q-byzanz-32#explanation: At his baptism Boris took the name of his godfather Michael III and later brought the disciples of Cyril and Methodius into his country.
q-byzanz-33#question: What epithet is Emperor Basil II known by?
q-byzanz-33#explanation: Basil II subjugated the Bulgarian Empire in decades of war; the epithet is attested only later.
q-byzanz-34#question: According to the chronicler Skylitzes, what did Basil II do with the Bulgarian prisoners after the battle of Kleidion in 1014?
q-byzanz-34#choices.1: He settled them in Asia Minor
q-byzanz-34#choices.3: He released them for a ransom
q-byzanz-34#explanation: According to Skylitzes, some 15,000 prisoners were blinded and sent back to Tsar Samuel; the number is probably exaggerated.
q-byzanz-35#question: What was the name of the Byzantine emperors' bodyguard made up of Scandinavians and Rus?
q-byzanz-35#explanation: The Varangian Guard arose at the end of the 10th century from an army that Vladimir of Kyiv had sent to Basil II.
q-byzanz-36#question: Which dynasty provided the Byzantine emperors from 867 to 1056?
q-byzanz-36#explanation: The Macedonian dynasty founded by Basil I led the empire into a new golden age.
q-byzanz-37#question: Which year is regarded as a symbol of the split between the Eastern and Western churches?
q-byzanz-37#explanation: In 1054 papal legates and the patriarch of Constantinople excommunicated each other.
q-byzanz-38#question: Which disputed question was among the causes of the schism of 1054?
q-byzanz-38#explanation: The Latin church had added the word "Filioque" ("and the Son") to the Creed, which the Eastern church rejected.
q-byzanz-39#question: When were the mutual excommunications of 1054 lifted?
q-byzanz-39#explanation: Pope Paul VI and Patriarch Athenagoras lifted the excommunications in 1965; the separation of the churches nevertheless continues.
q-byzanz-40#question: Who defeated the Byzantine emperor Romanos IV at Manzikert in 1071?
q-byzanz-40#explanation: Sultan Alp Arslan took the emperor prisoner; afterwards Turkish groups advanced deep into Asia Minor.
q-byzanz-41#question: Which southern Italian city, the last Byzantine stronghold in Italy, did the Normans capture in 1071?
q-byzanz-41#explanation: With the fall of Bari in the same year as Manzikert, Byzantine rule in Italy came to an end.
q-byzanz-42#question: Which Byzantine emperor asked the West for military help and so contributed to the First Crusade?
q-byzanz-42#explanation: Alexios I asked for mercenaries against the Seljuks; in response Pope Urban II called for a crusade in 1095.
q-byzanz-43#question: What is the name of the historical work in which Anna Komnene described her father's reign?
q-byzanz-43#explanation: The Alexiad, about Alexios I, is a principal source for the First Crusade from the Byzantine point of view.
q-byzanz-44#question: What right did Venetian merchants receive through the privilege of Alexios I?
q-byzanz-44#choices.0: Duty-free trade in almost all ports of the empire
q-byzanz-44#choices.1: The right to mint their own coins in the empire
q-byzanz-44#choices.2: Sole possession of the island of Crete
q-byzanz-44#choices.3: A seat on the imperial council
q-byzanz-44#explanation: In return for naval help against the Normans, the Venetians could trade free of duties and received their own quarter in Constantinople.
q-byzanz-45#question: Which city did the armies of the Fourth Crusade capture and sack in 1204?
q-byzanz-45#explanation: Instead of going to the Holy Land, the crusader army marched on Constantinople and plundered the Christian capital.
q-byzanz-46#question: Which Doge of Venice played a leading role in the Fourth Crusade?
q-byzanz-46#explanation: The aged and almost blind Enrico Dandolo accompanied the army and secured a large share of the spoils for Venice.
q-byzanz-47#question: Which famous works of art did the Venetians take from the Hippodrome of Constantinople to Venice in 1204?
q-byzanz-47#explanation: The four horses long adorned the façade of St Mark's Basilica; the originals are now in its museum.
q-byzanz-48#question: From which Greek successor state was Constantinople recaptured in 1261?
q-byzanz-48#explanation: Troops of Michael VIII Palaiologos, emperor of Nicaea, took the city in July 1261.
q-byzanz-49#question: Which dynasty ruled the Byzantine Empire from 1261 to 1453?
q-byzanz-49#explanation: The Palaiologan dynasty founded by Michael VIII was the empire's last.
q-byzanz-50#question: What did the Council of Ferrara and Florence decide in 1439?
q-byzanz-50#choices.2: A union of the Eastern and Western churches, which was largely rejected in Byzantium
q-byzanz-50#choices.3: The return of the treasures looted in 1204
q-byzanz-50#explanation: Emperor John VIII hoped the union would bring help against the Ottomans, but clergy and people largely rejected it.
q-byzanz-51#question: Which gold coin was the stable currency of the Byzantine Empire for centuries?
q-byzanz-51#explanation: The solidus introduced by Constantine kept its gold content until the 11th century and was sought after throughout the Mediterranean.
q-byzanz-52#question: Which mountain in northern Greece became the centre of Orthodox monasticism from the 10th century?
q-byzanz-52#explanation: In 963 the monastery of Great Lavra was founded on Athos; to this day monks live there in some twenty monasteries.
q-ozeanien-pazifik-01#question: In which present-day territory is the site after which the Lapita culture is named?
q-ozeanien-pazifik-01#explanation: The Lapita culture is named after a site in New Caledonia where its characteristic pottery was found.
q-ozeanien-pazifik-02#question: What is the main feature by which archaeologists recognize the Lapita culture?
q-ozeanien-pazifik-02#explanation: The hallmark of the Lapita culture is pottery with finely stamped geometric patterns.
q-ozeanien-pazifik-03#question: Which island groups did Lapita seafarers reach between about 1000 and 800 BC?
q-ozeanien-pazifik-03#choices.2: New Zealand and the Chatham Islands
q-ozeanien-pazifik-03#explanation: Fiji, Tonga and Samoa formed the western edge of Polynesia, where Polynesian culture then developed.
q-ozeanien-pazifik-04#question: Around what time did Polynesians reach New Zealand?
q-ozeanien-pazifik-04#explanation: Radiocarbon dates show that East Polynesian settlers reached New Zealand around 1250 to 1300.
q-ozeanien-pazifik-05#question: Who gave the Pacific Ocean its name?
q-ozeanien-pazifik-05#explanation: After the stormy passage through the Strait of Magellan in 1520, Magellan called the ocean the "Pacific", the peaceful sea.
q-ozeanien-pazifik-06#question: What are the large stone figures on Rapa Nui called?
q-ozeanien-pazifik-06#explanation: The moai represent revered ancestors; pukao is the name for the red topknots on some of the figures.
q-ozeanien-pazifik-07#question: From which crater does the stone of most moai come?
q-ozeanien-pazifik-07#explanation: Most moai were carved from the tuff of the Rano Raraku crater, where many unfinished figures still lie.
q-ozeanien-pazifik-08#question: Which island did Magellan's ships reach in March 1521 after crossing the Pacific?
q-ozeanien-pazifik-08#explanation: On 6 March 1521 the fleet reached Guam in the Marianas after more than three months at sea.
q-ozeanien-pazifik-09#question: Which island did Abel Tasman sight in November 1642 and name Van Diemen's Land?
q-ozeanien-pazifik-09#choices.2: The South Island of New Zealand
q-ozeanien-pazifik-09#explanation: Tasman named the island after the governor-general of the East India Company; later it was given his own name.
q-ozeanien-pazifik-10#question: On whose behalf did Abel Tasman sail in 1642?
q-ozeanien-pazifik-10#explanation: The East India Company sent Tasman out from Batavia to explore the supposed Southern Land.
q-ozeanien-pazifik-11#choices.0: A Māori chief who negotiated the Treaty of Waitangi
q-ozeanien-pazifik-11#choices.2: A priest and navigator from Raʻiātea who sailed with Cook
q-ozeanien-pazifik-11#choices.3: An Aboriginal man who travelled to England with Arthur Phillip
q-ozeanien-pazifik-11#explanation: Tupaia accompanied Cook from 1769, drew a chart of some 70 islands and interpreted in New Zealand.
q-ozeanien-pazifik-12#question: In which year did the First Fleet reach Australia?
q-ozeanien-pazifik-12#explanation: The eleven ships of the First Fleet reached Botany Bay in January 1788 and founded the colony at Sydney Cove.
q-ozeanien-pazifik-13#question: Who was the first governor of New South Wales?
q-ozeanien-pazifik-13#explanation: Arthur Phillip led the First Fleet to Australia and governed the colony until 1792.
q-ozeanien-pazifik-14#question: Where did Arthur Phillip have the British flag raised on 26 January 1788?
q-ozeanien-pazifik-14#choices.2: At Sydney Cove in Port Jackson
q-ozeanien-pazifik-14#explanation: Because Botany Bay seemed unsuitable, the fleet moved on to Port Jackson, where Sydney was founded.
q-ozeanien-pazifik-15#question: What was the colony of New South Wales mainly intended for at first?
q-ozeanien-pazifik-15#choices.0: As a base for the spice trade
q-ozeanien-pazifik-15#choices.1: As a penal colony for convicted criminals
q-ozeanien-pazifik-15#choices.2: As a mission station for the Pacific islands
q-ozeanien-pazifik-15#explanation: After losing its American colonies, Britain transported convicts to Australia.
q-ozeanien-pazifik-16#question: What struck the Eora around Sydney particularly hard in April 1789?
q-ozeanien-pazifik-16#choices.2: The arrival of a second fleet
q-ozeanien-pazifik-16#explanation: The epidemic, usually identified as smallpox, killed about half of the Aboriginal people in the area; its origin is disputed.
q-ozeanien-pazifik-17#choices.0: A leader of armed resistance near Parramatta
q-ozeanien-pazifik-17#choices.1: A Wangal man who mediated between the Eora and the colonists
q-ozeanien-pazifik-17#choices.2: A missionary of the London Missionary Society
q-ozeanien-pazifik-17#choices.3: A convict who was the first to find gold
q-ozeanien-pazifik-17#explanation: Bennelong was captured in 1789, later became an important intermediary and travelled to England with Phillip in 1792.
q-ozeanien-pazifik-18#question: Which Bidjigal man led resistance against the colonists near Sydney from about 1790?
q-ozeanien-pazifik-18#explanation: Pemulwuy led raids on farms near Parramatta and on the Hawkesbury River for more than a decade until he was shot in 1802.
q-ozeanien-pazifik-19#question: What were seafarers from Makassar looking for on the northern coast of Australia?
q-ozeanien-pazifik-19#explanation: The Macassans gathered and dried trepang, which was prized in China as a delicacy and medicine.
q-ozeanien-pazifik-20#question: What is the usual English name for the Aboriginal world view according to which ancestral beings created the land?
q-ozeanien-pazifik-20#explanation: The Dreaming is not a closed past but is present in places, songs and ceremonies.
q-ozeanien-pazifik-21#choices.0: Trade routes of the Macassan seafarers
q-ozeanien-pazifik-21#choices.1: Hymns of the missionaries on Tahiti
q-ozeanien-pazifik-21#choices.2: Song cycles describing the paths of ancestral beings across the land
q-ozeanien-pazifik-21#choices.3: Sea charts made of palm ribs and shells
q-ozeanien-pazifik-21#explanation: Songlines link songs, places and stories of the Dreaming and also served as guides over long distances.
q-ozeanien-pazifik-22#question: What does the "Coming of the Light" festival in the Torres Strait commemorate?
q-ozeanien-pazifik-22#choices.0: The arrival of Christian missionaries in 1871
q-ozeanien-pazifik-22#explanation: On 1 July 1871 missionaries of the London Missionary Society landed on Erub; the day is still celebrated.
q-ozeanien-pazifik-23#question: What are the fortified settlements of the Māori called?
q-ozeanien-pazifik-23#explanation: Pā usually stood on hills or headlands and were protected by ditches, banks and palisades; a marae is a meeting ground.
q-ozeanien-pazifik-24#question: Which giant flightless birds did New Zealand's first settlers hunt to extinction?
q-ozeanien-pazifik-24#explanation: The moa were wiped out within roughly one to two centuries of human arrival.
q-ozeanien-pazifik-25#question: In Māori tradition, what is the name of the homeland of their ancestors?
q-ozeanien-pazifik-25#explanation: Tradition tells of the voyage from Hawaiki in canoes such as Tainui and Te Arawa; Aotearoa is the Māori name for New Zealand.
q-ozeanien-pazifik-26#question: Which crop from South America is considered evidence of early contact between Polynesians and South America?
q-ozeanien-pazifik-26#explanation: The sweet potato originated in South America and was already widespread in Polynesia before Europeans arrived; the details of the contacts are disputed.
q-ozeanien-pazifik-27#question: Who united the Hawaiian Islands into a kingdom?
q-ozeanien-pazifik-27#explanation: Kamehameha I conquered most of the islands in 1795; in 1810 Kauaʻi also submitted.
q-ozeanien-pazifik-28#question: Which ruler submitted to Kamehameha without a fight in 1810?
q-ozeanien-pazifik-28#explanation: Kaumualiʻi, ruler of Kauaʻi and Niʻihau, acknowledged Kamehameha's overlordship in 1810, completing the unification.
q-ozeanien-pazifik-29#question: Which woman brought about the abolition of the kapu system in Hawaiʻi in 1819?
q-ozeanien-pazifik-29#explanation: Kaʻahumanu, the most influential wife of Kamehameha I, persuaded the young king to break the eating prohibitions in public.
q-ozeanien-pazifik-30#question: Which prohibition did King Liholiho break in public in 1819 to end the kapu system?
q-ozeanien-pazifik-30#choices.0: The ban on entering sacred volcanoes
q-ozeanien-pazifik-30#choices.1: The ban on fishing during spawning season
q-ozeanien-pazifik-30#choices.2: The ban on men and women eating together
q-ozeanien-pazifik-30#choices.3: The ban on wearing feather cloaks
q-ozeanien-pazifik-30#explanation: Liholiho ate with women at a feast; afterwards he had temples destroyed and images of the gods burned.
q-ozeanien-pazifik-31#question: Which queen was overthrown in Hawaiʻi in 1893?
q-ozeanien-pazifik-31#explanation: Liliʻuokalani was overthrown in January 1893 by American businessmen backed by US Marines.
q-ozeanien-pazifik-32#question: In which year did the United States annex Hawaiʻi?
q-ozeanien-pazifik-32#explanation: Congress approved annexation in July 1898; in 1959 Hawaiʻi became the 50th state.
q-ozeanien-pazifik-33#question: Who overthrew the Hawaiian monarchy in 1893?
q-ozeanien-pazifik-33#choices.1: American businessmen and planters backed by US Marines
q-ozeanien-pazifik-33#explanation: A "Committee of Safety" of businessmen declared a provisional government after US Marines had come ashore.
q-ozeanien-pazifik-34#question: Which song was written by Queen Liliʻuokalani?
q-ozeanien-pazifik-34#explanation: Liliʻuokalani wrote many songs, including "Aloha ʻOe"; the words of "Hawaiʻi Ponoʻī" were written by her brother Kalākaua.
q-ozeanien-pazifik-35#question: In which year was the Treaty of Waitangi signed?
q-ozeanien-pazifik-35#explanation: On 6 February 1840 William Hobson and Māori chiefs signed the treaty at Waitangi.
q-ozeanien-pazifik-36#question: Who signed the Treaty of Waitangi on behalf of the British Crown?
q-ozeanien-pazifik-36#explanation: Hobson had been instructed to obtain the chiefs' consent to British rule and became governor in 1841.
q-ozeanien-pazifik-37#question: What did the Māori version of the Treaty of Waitangi guarantee with "tino rangatiratanga"?
q-ozeanien-pazifik-37#choices.0: The cession of all sovereignty to the Crown
q-ozeanien-pazifik-37#choices.2: Full authority over lands, villages and treasures
q-ozeanien-pazifik-37#explanation: Under the Māori version the chiefs ceded only "kāwanatanga" and retained "tino rangatiratanga"; this lies at the heart of the dispute over the treaty.
q-ozeanien-pazifik-38#question: Which Ngāpuhi chief travelled to England in 1820 and afterwards waged campaigns with muskets?
q-ozeanien-pazifik-38#explanation: In England Hongi Hika met King George IV, and on the return journey he acquired large numbers of muskets in Sydney.
q-ozeanien-pazifik-39#question: What are the wars between Māori tribes in the early 19th century, in which firearms were first used, called?
q-ozeanien-pazifik-39#explanation: In the Musket Wars Māori tribes fought one another; the New Zealand Wars, by contrast, were fought by Māori against British troops.
q-ozeanien-pazifik-40#question: Which chief repeatedly cut down the British flagstaff at Kororāreka from 1844 onwards?
q-ozeanien-pazifik-40#explanation: Hōne Heke's protest against British rule led in 1845 to the first of the New Zealand Wars.
q-ozeanien-pazifik-41#question: Who was chosen as the first Māori king in 1858?
q-ozeanien-pazifik-41#explanation: The King Movement chose the elderly Waikato chief in order to protect land from sale; his son Tāwhiao succeeded him in 1860.
q-ozeanien-pazifik-42#question: What happened to the land of many Māori tribes after the Waikato War of 1863/64?
q-ozeanien-pazifik-42#choices.0: The government bought it at market prices
q-ozeanien-pazifik-42#choices.2: It was placed under the protection of the King Movement
q-ozeanien-pazifik-42#choices.3: It was handed over to the missions
q-ozeanien-pazifik-42#explanation: Under a law of 1863 the government confiscated more than a million hectares of Māori land.
q-ozeanien-pazifik-43#question: What triggered mass immigration to Australia in 1851?
q-ozeanien-pazifik-43#choices.2: Gold discoveries in New South Wales and Victoria
q-ozeanien-pazifik-43#choices.3: The building of a railway across the continent
q-ozeanien-pazifik-43#explanation: After the finds at Bathurst, Ballarat and Bendigo, Victoria's population rose to over half a million within ten years.
q-ozeanien-pazifik-44#question: What was the rebellion at the Eureka Stockade in 1854 directed against?
q-ozeanien-pazifik-44#choices.0: Expensive mining licences on the goldfields
q-ozeanien-pazifik-44#explanation: The miners at Ballarat were outraged by the licence fees; the rebellion was suppressed but led to reforms.
q-ozeanien-pazifik-45#question: When was the Commonwealth of Australia founded?
q-ozeanien-pazifik-45#explanation: On 1 January 1901 the six Australian colonies united as a federation.
q-ozeanien-pazifik-46#question: Who was Australia's first prime minister?
q-ozeanien-pazifik-46#explanation: Edmund Barton led the first federal government from 1901 to 1903 and then became a judge of the High Court.
q-ozeanien-pazifik-47#question: Which policy did the Immigration Restriction Act of 1901 establish?
q-ozeanien-pazifik-47#choices.2: The return of land to Aboriginal people
q-ozeanien-pazifik-47#explanation: The law was designed above all to keep out immigrants from Asia and the Pacific and remained in force in modified form for decades.
q-ozeanien-pazifik-48#question: Which king gave Tonga a constitution in 1875?
q-ozeanien-pazifik-48#explanation: George Tupou I united Tonga in 1845; his constitution of 1875 helped the country avoid colonization.
q-ozeanien-pazifik-49#question: What were the sacred kings of Tonga called, whose line according to tradition began in the 10th century?
q-ozeanien-pazifik-49#explanation: The Tuʻi Tonga were regarded as descendants of the god Tangaloa; from the 15th century they left secular power to other lines.
q-ozeanien-pazifik-50#question: Which missionary society sent missionaries to Tahiti on the ship Duff in 1797?
q-ozeanien-pazifik-50#choices.2: The American Board of Commissioners for Foreign Missions
q-ozeanien-pazifik-50#explanation: The London Missionary Society began the Protestant mission in Polynesia on Tahiti in 1797.
q-ozeanien-pazifik-51#question: What does the term "blackbirding" refer to?
q-ozeanien-pazifik-51#choices.0: The recruitment of Pacific workers by deception or force
q-ozeanien-pazifik-51#choices.2: The banning of tattoos by missionaries
q-ozeanien-pazifik-51#choices.3: The trade in bird feathers for cloaks
q-ozeanien-pazifik-51#explanation: Tens of thousands of Melanesians were recruited in this way for plantations in Queensland, Fiji and Samoa.
q-ozeanien-pazifik-52#question: From which languages does the word "taboo" come?
q-ozeanien-pazifik-52#explanation: James Cook brought the word "tapu" from Tonga to Europe; it denotes what is sacred and forbidden.
q-russland-osteuropa-01#question: According to the Primary Chronicle, whom did the tribes around Novgorod invite to rule them in 862?
q-russland-osteuropa-01#explanation: The Primary Chronicle from the early 12th century tells of Rurik's invitation; how much of it is historical is uncertain.
q-russland-osteuropa-02#question: Which city did Oleg make the centre of the Rus around 882?
q-russland-osteuropa-02#explanation: Oleg travelled down the Dnieper from Novgorod, conquered Kyiv and, according to the chronicle, called it the "mother of the cities of the Rus".
q-russland-osteuropa-03#question: Which princess ruled for her son Sviatoslav and was baptized in Constantinople around 957?
q-russland-osteuropa-03#explanation: Olga, the widow of Prince Igor, was the first ruler of the Rus to adopt Christianity.
q-russland-osteuropa-04#question: Whom did Volodymyr I marry in connection with his baptism in 988?
q-russland-osteuropa-04#choices.1: Theophanu, the widow of Emperor Otto II
q-russland-osteuropa-04#choices.2: Anna, the sister of the Byzantine emperor Basil II
q-russland-osteuropa-04#choices.3: Ingegerd, the daughter of the Swedish king
q-russland-osteuropa-04#explanation: The marriage to the emperor's sister Anna tied Kievan Rus closely to Byzantium.
q-russland-osteuropa-05#question: What is the name of the oldest law code of the Rus, whose first version goes back to Yaroslav the Wise?
q-russland-osteuropa-05#explanation: The Russkaya Pravda limited blood feud and set fines for crimes.
q-russland-osteuropa-06#question: Which daughter of Yaroslav the Wise became queen of France?
q-russland-osteuropa-06#explanation: Anna married King Henry I of France in 1051; her sisters became queens of Norway and Hungary.
q-russland-osteuropa-07#question: In which year did the Mongols conquer and destroy Kyiv?
q-russland-osteuropa-07#explanation: In December 1240 Kyiv fell to Batu's army; afterwards the city lost its importance for a long time.
q-russland-osteuropa-08#question: Where was the capital of the Golden Horde?
q-russland-osteuropa-08#choices.1: At Sarai on the lower Volga
q-russland-osteuropa-08#choices.2: At Kazan on the middle Volga
q-russland-osteuropa-08#explanation: Sarai on the lower Volga was the residence of the khans, to whom the Russian princes had to travel.
q-russland-osteuropa-09#choices.0: A tax paid only by merchants in Novgorod
q-russland-osteuropa-09#choices.1: A wooden peasant house in the northern Rus
q-russland-osteuropa-09#choices.2: An electoral body of the Cossacks on the Dnieper
q-russland-osteuropa-09#choices.3: A charter from the khan confirming a prince in his office
